top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu alone (P001) is the only awarding proposal on the slate and the best-supported literary option. On the common criteria, public knowledge of Blinding (the Orbitor sequence) and Solenoid points to a distinctive visionary voice, very large patterned structures in which scale does formal work, and memory, the body and dream treated as one metaphysical project. Solenoid is widely regarded as a late culmination, so premature judgment is not the issue. The round-2 exchange settled the citation on the prose, with poetry named only as an origin, since translated coverage of the poetry is thin. Unresolved reservations remain: whether the late novels deepen their image systems or recirculate them, how much of the Romanian prose's density and musicality survives translation, and whether reinvention of a language or genre should outweigh large-scale visionary construction. These reflect limits of access and translation, not findings against the work. They do not justify P000, which would withhold the prize from a writer whose major work appears sufficient for a recommendation. I have not read the corpus for this exercise or independently verified any source, and unanimity in the opening ballots is not treated as merit.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented connection to Mircea Cărtărescu. As chair I wrote the round-1 summary and support B026, which is disclosed and not adjudicated. My scholarly interests (modern poetry, the fragment, exile literature, Celan) are context, not evidence of preference.
